reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence - 90.2% (37/41) achieved successful engraftment, demonstrating the CD34+ selected stem cells reached and engaged the hematopoietic system. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Good evidence - immune reconstitution occurred as shown by progressive increases in CD3/4 and CD3/8 T-cell counts from day 28 to day 90, indicating successful hematopoietic reconstitution. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Moderate success - 65.9% (27/41) achieved 1-year relapse-free survival, which appears reasonable for high-risk hematologic malignancies, though no comparator or statistical significance testing provided. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analysis reported to assess differential responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design without control group makes it difficult to assess true efficacy; safety concerns with 2 GVHD deaths and multiple toxicities may have limited optimal dosing/treatment delivery.
